reason: The passage depicts Moses, the leader of the Hebrew people, responding to their fear and complaints about being pursued by Pharaoh's army. When the Israelites express their distress—saying it would have been better to remain in servitude in Egypt than to die in the wilderness—Moses does not acknowledge accountability for their dire circumstances. Instead, he tells them not to fear and assures them that God will deliver them (וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אֶל־ הָעָם אַל־ תִּירָאוּ). He redirects responsibility to divine intervention rather than taking personal responsibility for the state of the people. Additionally, Pharaoh (another leader figure in the passage) expresses regret at having released Israel but does not accept accountability for his decision—he simply pursues them militarily. Neither leader explicitly acknowledges responsibility for the Hebrew people's suffering and precarious position.
story: The Pharaoh chases after the Hebrews
